Baelen Bonecloak is a dwarf in the Dread Hollow. He is trapped in the Bibberbang Grotto to the northwest of the Myconid Colony as related during the ⁠Find the Mushroom Picker quest given by his wife,  Derryth Bonecloak. If he survives this encounter, he eventually relocates to Bonecloak's Apothecary in the Lower City in Act Three.
“
Can't be too careful in these parts. Bibberbang's the least of it.
„
— Baelen Bonecloak

Overview

Baelen and  Derryth Bonecloak run Bonecloak's Apothecary in Baldur's Gate. Needing to restock one of the more popular and expensive items at their store,  Noblestalk, they travelled to the Underdark. The two set up a temporary camp in Ebonlake Grotto with a myconid colony, and Derryth sent Baelen off to collect the mushroom.

Involvement

Act One

Baelen is trapped in the middle of the Bibberbang Grotto to the northwest of the Myconid Colony. He has been separated from his  Baelen's Pack and needs the party's help retrieving the  Scroll of Misty Step to safely escape the explosive Bibberbang field. While Baelen's natural resistance to poison would normally help him with the noxious fumes of the Bibberbang, his dropped torch will set their spores alight if triggered, and cause a chain of explosions across the entire field that would no doubt kill him along with any unprepared adventurers.

The party can try to carefully retrieve his scroll to throw or hand to him or throw his pack to him (or have him use their own scroll if they happen to have one) so he can teleport out of the field. Alternatively, picking up the torch (or extinguishing it) and providing Baelen with healing is likely enough to have him survive should the mushrooms be agitated. Once he is safely out of the field, Baelen displays some confusion and acts as if he and the party were in the middle of a conversation he forgot about. Alternatively  Glut or a  Mage Hand can traverse the Bibberbang without triggering any fumes, and can either to throw Baelen's Pack to the party or to Baelen.[2] After a brief exchange of words, he gives the party a  Scroll of Invisibility as thanks and runs back to his wife.

Once they are reunited, Baelen rests near their tent. When asked how he got into his predicament, he recalls (with some difficulty) he was attempting to pick Noblestalk when the ledge he was on gave way and deposited him in the middle of the field. He cannot explain very well why his mind is how it is now and directs any inquirers to Derryth. Derryth herself is cold when she speaks of Baelen, and expresses more concern about how he has not retrieved  Noblestalk than how he almost died. They have been married over eighty years and their first seventy were not pleasant, as Baelen was a heavy drinker and abusive towards her, drawing attention to her scars. According to their Deep Rothé, Baelen used to kick him before but treats him better now. The Rothé even expresses he misses Baelen and his scratches. Derryth concludes by saying she will likely be sending Baelen out again to pick Noblestalk, if not doing it herself.[3][4]

If the party have the Noblestalk, Baelen is happy for Derryth as it helps them keep their shop, Bonecloak's Apothecary in Baldur's Gate afloat. He can be given the Noblestalk directly once the party learns that it could restore his mind, and he gladly consumes it so that he can help his wife with the shop. Once he is restored, however, his attitude shifts back to his old self, and he wastes no time in berating his wife for using him as a workhorse when he was not of right mind. Furthermore, the couple's Deep Rothé comments how he sounds different now, like his old self, his Angry self" and that he hopes Baelen does not start kicking him again. Baelen thanks the party and invites them to visit him at his shop when they get there, while Derryth expresses her disgust at the party and refuses to trade, telling them to leave her alone.

Should Baelen die in the Bibberbang field, Derryth shows more grief about him failing to do his job than about his death. In contrast, if Derryth is killed before Baelen is reunited with her, he mourns over her body, saying he is nothing without her. If the party admits to killing her, he turns hostile. Otherwise he laments that he should not have left her alone, and he cannot be given the Noblestalk.

Act Three

At Bonecloak's Apothecary, if he was not given the Noblestalk, Baelen cheerfully tends to the shop, greeting any customers who approach. Going through  Derryth's journal upstairs in this iteration reveals that, at some point in the past, Derryth was especially sick of Baelen's drinking and abuse after their return from one Underdark expedition and vowed in writing if he hits me again, he's going to find some  Wyvern Toxin in his porridge the next morning, an outburst she herself is surprised at later on, amending that she should hide her journal lest people get the wrong idea.

If Baelen was given the Noblestalk previously, he is instead alone at his shop, having taken over the inventory that Derryth was previously selling. It appears Derryth ran off one night, fearing his wrath for using him. However, seeing as how there are Absolutists in the city and a murderer is terrorizing the citizenry, there is not much for him to complain about as he has not had any unfortunate run-ins with them so far. He even goes as far to joke that, with any luck, the trouble will end up finding Derryth instead. Should the party condemn him, he states that it is what he does to make ends meet, assuming that the party has likewise not been able to get to Baldur's Gate without getting their hands dirty. In this iteration, Derryth's journal instead talks about how she regrets how the years she has spent suffering under her husband had hardened her heart and made her as cold as Baelen is. And while she had been able to put up with him in the past, the simple return of Baelen's old self has killed her spirit more than any of his past abuse ever did, so she has resolved to leave him.

Should Baelen not survive his Underdark expedition, Derryth is alone at Bonecloak's. While she is outwardly as abrasive as ever, she turns melancholy when thinking of her late husband, stating that they both deserved better than how their lives turned out. She reckons that Baelen's soul found its way to the  City of Judgement, wasting away unclaimed as a faithless.[5] Her journal in this iteration concurs that Derryth dearly misses her husband, and she has been thinking of using their own merchandise to cope, though she rebuffs herself, stating that doing so was the very reason Baelen lost his own mind.

Finally, if Derryth was killed in the Underdark and Baelen left alone, or if both Baelen and Derryth died in Act One, Bonecloak's Apothecary is closed, with a simple  Pinned-up Note left out front, "Gone shroom hunting."

Speak with Dead

Baelen can be spoken to with  Speak with Dead.

  • Who are you?
    • Baelen Bonecloak
      Baelen... Bonecloak...
  • What was your profession?
    • Baelen Bonecloak
      Alchemist... shop... in Baldur's Gate...
  • How did you die?
    • Baelen Bonecloak
      Hunting... noblestalk... fell... bibberbang... explosion... (If Baelen dies from a bibberbang explosion)
    • Baelen Bonecloak
      Can't... remember... just... nothing... (If Baelen does not die from a bibberbang explosion and does not see his killer)
  • Why were you in the Underdark?
    • Baelen Bonecloak
      Hunting... ingredients... nobestalk... with my love...
      • Where is your wife?
        • Baelen Bonecloak
          Derryth... with myconids... helping... gnome...
  • Did you have any valuables?
    • Baelen Bonecloak
      Home... shop... Baldur's Gate... Bonecloak's...

Notes and references

  1. ↑ While Baelen shows up on the minimap as a Trader, he only becomes available as one in Act Three if given the Noblestalk.
  2. ↑ It seems to be possible to throw the empty pack back to Baelen, and he still somehow "finds" the scroll that he needs to teleport out and rewards the party with a  Scroll of Invisibility)
  3. ↑ "My husband. Eighty soggin' years together, and he leaves me in the lurch like this."
  4. ↑ "Sure I did. Before he could do me any worse damage than he did for the first seventy years of our marriage."
  5. ↑ "We both of us deserved better than life gave us. Now he's off in the City of Judgement, probably wasting away unclaimed, the old heathen. And I'm here. Alone."
